unfortunately.ex: Unfortunately, the museum is closed today.
unfortunately.def: Used to say that something is sad or disappointing.

unhealthy.def: Not good for your health; also, not well.

uniform.ex: Pupils must wear a school uniform.
uniform.def: A special set of clothes worn by all members of a group, such as students or police officers.

unify.def: To bring together to form one unit.
unify.ex: The new leader promised to unify the country.

unique.def: Being the only one of its kind; very special.

unite.def: To join together to act as a group.
unite.ex: The two countries united against the threat.

universe.def: Everything that exists, including the earth, the stars and all of space.

university.def: A place of higher education where students study for degrees and research is done.
university.ex: She is studying law at university.

unless.ex: You will fail unless you study harder.

unprecedented.ex: The city has seen unprecedented growth.

until.ex: The library is open until eight o'clock.

upbringing.def: The way a child is cared for and taught while growing up.

update.def: To make something more modern or add the latest information to it.

upgrade.def: To improve something by replacing it with a newer or better version.
upgrade.ex: The airport will upgrade its security systems.

upheaval.ex: The move caused great upheaval for the family.
upheaval.def: A big change that causes a lot of confusion or worry.

upload.ex: Upload your essay to the website before Friday.
upload.def: To send information or files from your computer or phone to the internet.

upset.def: To make someone feel unhappy or worried.

urban.def: Relating to a town or city.
urban.ex: Urban areas have more pollution than rural ones.

urbanisation.ex: Rapid urbanisation has led to traffic congestion.
urbanisation.def: The process by which more people come to live in towns and cities.

urge.def: To strongly encourage someone to do something.
urge.ex: Doctors urge people to stop smoking.

urgent.def: Needing to be dealt with immediately.

useful.ex: A dictionary is a useful tool for learners.
useful.def: Helpful for doing or achieving something.

user.def: A person who uses a product, service or machine.
user.ex: The app has over a million users.

utilise.ex: We need to utilise renewable energy sources.

utmost.ex: Safety is of the utmost importance.

vacancy.ex: There is a vacancy for a part-time assistant.
vacancy.def: A job that is available; also, a free room in a hotel.

vacation.def: A holiday (mainly US); also, the time when universities are closed.
vacation.ex: Students work during the summer vacation.

vaccination.ex: Vaccination protects children from serious diseases.
vaccination.def: Giving someone a vaccine to protect them from a disease.

vaccine.def: A substance put into the body to protect it from a disease.
vaccine.ex: Scientists developed the vaccine in record time.

valid.def: Legally acceptable; also, based on good reasons.
valid.ex: Your passport must be valid for six months.

valuable.def: Worth a lot of money; also, very useful.
valuable.ex: Work experience is valuable for students.

value.def: How much something is worth; also, the importance of something.

vandalism.def: Deliberate damage to public or private property.
vandalism.ex: Vandalism is a problem in some city parks.

vary.ex: Prices vary from shop to shop.

vast.ex: A vast amount of food is wasted every year.

vegan.ex: She became a vegan five years ago.
vegan.def: A person who does not eat or use any animal products, such as meat, eggs or milk.

vegetable.def: A plant or part of a plant eaten as food, such as a carrot or a potato.
vegetable.ex: Eat plenty of fresh fruit and vegetables.

vegetarian.ex: My sister has been a vegetarian since she was twelve.
vegetarian.def: A person who does not eat meat or fish.

vegetation.def: Plants in general, especially those in a particular area.

vehicle.def: A machine such as a car, bus or lorry that carries people or goods.

verdict.def: The official decision made in a court about whether someone is guilty.

versatile.def: Able to do many different things, or to be used in many ways.

version.ex: The new version of the app is much faster.
version.def: A form of something that is slightly different from other forms.

vertical.ex: Draw a vertical line down the page.

via.def: Travelling through a place, or using a particular method or person.
via.ex: We flew to Sydney via Singapore.

viable.ex: Solar power is now a viable alternative to coal.

viewer.def: A person who watches television or a film.
viewer.ex: The programme attracted five million viewers.

viewpoint.def: A way of thinking about a subject; an opinion.
viewpoint.ex: Consider the problem from the viewpoint of the customer.

vigorous.def: Strong, active and full of energy.
vigorous.ex: Do at least 30 minutes of vigorous exercise.

village.ex: She grew up in a small village.
village.def: A small group of houses and other buildings in the countryside.

violate.def: To break a rule, law or agreement.

violation.ex: The company was fined for a violation of safety rules.
violation.def: The breaking of a law, rule or agreement.

violence.def: Behaviour that is intended to hurt or kill someone.
violence.ex: There has been an increase in violence on the streets.

violent.def: Using force to hurt or kill; also, very strong.

viral.def: Caused by a virus; also, spreading very quickly online.

virtual.def: Created by computers to seem real; also, almost complete.
virtual.ex: Virtual reality is used in training doctors.

virus.def: A tiny living thing that causes illnesses such as flu; also, a program that damages computers.

visa.ex: You need a visa to work in the country.
visa.def: An official mark in a passport that allows you to enter or stay in a country.

vision.def: The ability to see; also, an idea of how the future could be.
vision.ex: She has a clear vision for the company.

visual.ex: Visual aids help students to learn.

vital.ex: Exercise is vital for good health.

vitamin.def: A natural substance in food that the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy.
vitamin.ex: Oranges are rich in vitamin C.

vivid.def: Very clear and detailed; also, (of colours) bright.
vivid.ex: She has vivid memories of her childhood.

vocation.def: A type of work that you feel strongly suited to and want to do.
vocation.ex: Teaching is a vocation, not just a job.

vocational.def: Teaching the skills needed for a particular job.
vocational.ex: Vocational courses prepare students for work.

volcanic.ex: Volcanic eruptions can affect the climate.
volcanic.def: Caused or produced by a mountain that throws out hot melted rock.

volcano.def: A mountain with a hole at the top through which hot melted rock and gas can escape.
volcano.ex: The volcano erupted after years of silence.

volume.def: The amount of space something fills, or the amount of something; also, how loud a sound is.
volume.ex: The volume of traffic has increased.

voluntary.def: Done because you choose to, not because you must; done without payment.
voluntary.ex: She does voluntary work at a hospital.

volunteer.def: To offer to do something without being paid or forced to.
volunteer.ex: She volunteers at the local hospital every weekend.

voter.def: A person who votes in an election.

voyage.ex: The voyage across the Atlantic took two weeks.
voyage.def: A long journey, especially by ship.

vulnerability.ex: The attack exposed the vulnerability of the computer system.

vulnerable.def: Easily harmed or hurt, physically or emotionally.
vulnerable.ex: Elderly people are vulnerable to the flu.

wage.def: Money paid to a worker, usually every week, for the work they do.

ward.def: A room in a hospital for patients; also, an area of a city that elects its own councillor.
ward.ex: The patient was moved to a different ward.

warn.def: To tell someone about a possible danger or problem.
warn.ex: Scientists warn that sea levels are rising.

waste.def: To use more of something than is needed, or to use it badly.

wealth.def: A large amount of money or possessions; also, a large amount of something.
wealth.ex: The country's wealth comes from oil.

wealthy.ex: Wealthy countries should help poorer ones.

weapon.def: A gun, knife or other object used to hurt people.
weapon.ex: Carrying a weapon is a crime.

website.def: A set of pages on the internet about a particular subject, company or person.
website.ex: You can book tickets on our website.

Wednesday.ex: The library is closed on Wednesday afternoons.
Wednesday.def: The day of the week after Tuesday and before Thursday.

welfare.def: Health, safety and happiness; also, help given by the government to people in need.
welfare.ex: The charity works to improve animal welfare.

wellbeing.def: The state of being healthy, happy and comfortable.

west.def: The direction where the sun sets.
west.ex: The town is about ten miles to the west of the city.

westernisation.def: The adoption of Western culture and ways of life.

wheat.ex: Bread is usually made from wheat flour.
wheat.def: A cereal plant whose grain is made into flour for bread and pasta.

whereas.def: While on the other hand; used to compare or contrast two facts.
whereas.ex: Some students prefer to study alone, whereas others prefer group work.

whereby.ex: They introduced a system whereby workers can choose their hours.

wherever.ex: You can sit wherever you like.

whether.def: If; used to show a choice between possibilities.
whether.ex: I am not sure whether the train has left.

while.def: During the time that; also, although.
while.ex: I listened to music while I studied.

whilst.def: During the time that; also, although (used mainly in British English).
whilst.ex: Some people prefer to study alone, whilst others learn better in groups.

wholesale.def: The selling of goods in large amounts to shops rather than to the public.
wholesale.ex: The shop buys its goods wholesale.

wholesome.def: Good for your health; also, morally good.

widespread.def: Existing or happening in many places or among many people.
widespread.ex: There is widespread support for the plan.

wildfire.ex: Wildfires have become more common in hot, dry summers.
wildfire.def: A large fire that spreads quickly through forests or countryside.

wildlife.def: Animals, birds and plants that live in natural conditions.
wildlife.ex: Pollution is a serious threat to wildlife.

winter.def: The coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.
winter.ex: Heating costs rise sharply in winter.

wireless.ex: The hotel offers free wireless internet.

wisdom.def: The ability to make good decisions based on knowledge and experience.
wisdom.ex: Older people can share their wisdom with the young.

wise.ex: It would be wise to book early.
wise.def: Showing good judgement and the benefit of experience.

witness.def: To see something happen, especially a crime or accident.

workforce.ex: Women now make up half of the workforce.
workforce.def: All the people who work in a company, industry or country.

workload.ex: Teachers complain about their heavy workload.
workload.def: The amount of work that a person has to do.

workplace.ex: Bullying in the workplace should not be tolerated.

workshop.def: A meeting where people learn about a subject by discussing it and doing activities; also, a room where things are made.
workshop.ex: The museum runs workshops for children.

worldwide.def: Existing or happening in every country; global.

worsen.def: To become or make something more bad or more serious.
worsen.ex: Air quality has worsened in recent years.

worship.def: Showing respect and love to a god, for example by praying.
worship.ex: The temple is a place of worship.

wound.def: An injury, especially a cut in the skin.
wound.ex: The wound took weeks to heal.

writing.def: The activity of creating texts; also, a text that someone has produced.
writing.ex: Academic writing needs a formal style.

yield.def: To produce a crop, profit or result; also, to give way.
yield.ex: The research yielded some surprising results.

youth.def: The period of life when someone is young; also, young people in general.

zealous.ex: He was a zealous supporter of the new policy.
zealous.def: Very enthusiastic and passionate about something.
